title: Preparation of magnetic nanoparticle integrated nanostructured lipid carriers for controlled delivery of ascorbyl palmitate
author: Kalaycioglu

steps.title: Prepare iron precursor solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.18 g FeSO₄·7H₂O in 1.75 mL ultrapure water and 0.34 g FeCl₃·6H₂O in 2 mL ultrapure water in separate vials, then combine the two solutions in a single vial.

steps.title: Co‑precipitate magnetite nanoparticles
steps.instruction: Prepare 0.8 g NaOH in 20 mL water; add this NaOH solution dropwise to the Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ mixture while stirring until the pH reaches 10. Add 80 µL oleic acid, continue mechanical stirring at room temperature for 1 h, then heat the emulsion to 95 °C at a rate of 2 °C min⁻¹, hold as needed, and cool back to room temperature. Adjust the pH to 5 using 35 % HNO₃.

steps.title: Wash and collect coated MNp
steps.instruction: Wash the precipitated particles four times with ultrapure water to remove salts, then wash once with acetone to eliminate residual water and excess oleic acid. Collect the purified oleic‑acid‑coated magnetite nanoparticle dispersion.

steps.title: Characterize MNp size and magnetization
steps.instruction: Measure particle diameter by Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS) (expected 16 ± 2 nm) and assess magnetic properties with a vibrating sample magnetometer at 25 °C over a field range of ±40 000 Oe (saturation magnetization ≈ 60 emu g⁻¹, no coercivity).

steps.title: Prepare lipid and aqueous phases
steps.instruction: In one vial (lipid phase) add 0.0665 g stearic acid and 31.8 µL oleic acid, then add 3 mL acetone and 3 mL ethanol; in a second vial (aqueous phase) add the required amount of Tween 80 (emulsifier). Heat both vials to 75 °C.

steps.title: Add active ingredients and form NLC
steps.instruction: If preparing AP‑MNLC, weigh 0.076 g ascorbyl palmitate (AP) and 0.021 mg magnetite nanoparticles and add them to the lipid phase after the ethanol has been added. When both phases reach 75 °C, inject the entire lipid phase into the aqueous phase in one motion using a glass syringe, then stir the mixture at 1000 rpm for 30 min.

steps.title: Cool and solidify NLCs
steps.instruction: Rapidly cool the stirred emulsion to 0 °C to solidify the nanostructured lipid carriers, yielding the final NLC or AP‑MNLC dispersion.

steps.title: Characterize NLC particle size
steps.instruction: Determine the size distribution of the NLCs using Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) and Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS) (expected diameters around 144 ± 11 nm for AP‑MNLC).

steps.title: Perform hyperthermia heating test
steps.instruction: Place 1.5 mL of the NLC dispersion in a centrifuge tube, insert the tube into the center of an 8‑turn copper coil (outer diameter 3.2 cm, inner diameter 2.5 cm) of the Ambrell Easy Heat induction heater, set the magnetic field to 47.7 kA m⁻¹ at 36 °C, and record the temperature rise using a fiber‑optic sensor while the coil operates within its 302–325 kHz frequency range (max 150 A).

steps.title: Conduct drug release assay
steps.instruction: Put 12 mL of NLC dispersion into a dialysis bag (MWCO 14 000) and immerse it in 80 mL phosphate‑buffered saline (pH 7.4) at 37 ± 1 °C with magnetic stirring at 50 rpm. At predetermined time points withdraw 500 µL of the external medium for analysis.

steps.title: Analyze released drug via UV‑vis and permanganometry
steps.instruction: Measure the withdrawn samples directly by UV‑vis spectroscopy (Thermo Scientific GENESYS 10S) at 525 nm after reacting 1 mL of each sample with 1 mL of 0.1 mg mL⁻¹ KMnO₄ solution (prepared in 5 M H₂SO₄) and incubating for 5 min at room temperature; calculate drug‑release percentage using the calibration curve and the formula Release % = (Amount released / Total encapsulated) × 100.
